decisions.reason: As a generic web service with relatively low carrying costs, it remains a cheap option to keep available while continuing to support the firm’s broader web-service offering.
This niche Austrian energy database likely requires ongoing data maintenance and, after several years, management would probably close it if demand has not clearly justified the upkeep.
A specialized peak-load determination service is costly to maintain relative to its narrow market, so by 2022 the firm would likely abandon it unless it had already shown strong traction.

An end-customer tariff database depends on continuous updates and regulatory relevance, making it the type of option a medium software firm would prune once its commercial value has largely been revealed.

Custom web services fit closely with the core business of a programming and consultancy firm, so management would be inclined to retain and redeploy resources around this offering rather than exit it.
A postal code lookup service is inexpensive to keep on the market and can complement other digital products, so the option value of retaining it is still favorable.
